sections.label: Committees made recommendations
sections.summary: The Committees together made close to 150 recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Committees, together, made close to 150 recommendations.

sections.label: Applications filed and international recognition
sections.summary: Close to 100 applications were filed with the Singapore Courts in a little more than a year, and Singapore was recognised as Most Improved Jurisdiction in June 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In a little more than a year, close to 100 applications under the new provisions have been filed with the Singapore Courts, which is a significant number within a short period of time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Our reforms have also garnered attention internationally, including Singapore being recognised as the "Most Improved Jurisdiction" at the inaugural Global Restructuring Review Awards in June 2017.

sections.label: Repeal of Bankruptcy and Companies Act provisions
sections.summary: If passed and in force, the Bankruptcy Act and corporate insolvency provisions of the Companies Act will be repealed, with amendments to about 70 other Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: If the Bill is passed and comes into force, the Bankruptcy Act will be repealed in its entirety; the provisions in the Companies Act relating to corporate insolvency and restructuring will be repealed; and necessary consequential and related amendments will be made to about 70 other Acts of Parliament.

sections.label: Streamlining administration of insufficient-asset cases
sections.summary: The new procedure aims to streamline public resources for cases with insufficient assets, with more than 100 companies as of 31 August 2018 having estimated realisable assets under S$1,000 each.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The impetus for this new procedure is to streamline the use of public resources and funds in administering cases where there are insufficient assets to fund even the administration of the liquidation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: There is a sizeable number of such cases and, to give Members a sense of the scale, as of 31 August 2018, there were more than 100 companies undergoing winding up by the Official Receiver, with estimated realisable assets of less than S$1,000 in each case.

sections.label: New wrongful trading provision
sections.summary: Clause 239 introduces a wrongful trading provision replacing sections 339 and 340 of the Companies Act, making knowing parties personally liable for debts incurred without reasonable prospect of full payment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Third, clause 239 introduces a new "wrongful trading" provision that replaces the old insolvent trading regime in sections 339 and 340, in particular, sections 339(3) and 340(2) of the Companies Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Under clause 239, therefore, a company trades wrongfully if the company incurs debts or liabilities without reasonable prospect of meeting them in full when the company is insolvent, or becomes insolvent as a result of the incurrence of such debt or liability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The new clause 239 empowers the Court to declare that any person who was a knowing party to the company trading wrongfully shall be personally liable and responsible for those debts or liabilities of the company.

sections.label: Regulation of insolvency practitioners
sections.summary: The Insolvency and Public Trustee's Office under MinLaw will regulate more than 300 insolvency practitioners under the new regime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: To raise standards and improve accountability, the Insolvency and Public Trustee’s Office under MinLaw will regulate more than 300 insolvency practitioners, who will fall under this new regime.

sections.label: Court approval of dissenting creditors
sections.summary: Clause 70 lets the Court approve a scheme of arrangement despite dissenting creditor classes if it is fair and equitable to them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Second, clause 70 empowers the Court to approve a scheme of arrangement despite there being dissenting classes of creditors, provided that the scheme is fair and equitable to the dissenting class.

sections.label: Company judicial management tool
sections.summary: Clause 94 is a new tool allowing a company to place itself into judicial management if creditors agree and support it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Turning to judicial management, clause 94 is a new tool which seeks to allow a company to place itself into judicial management provided that creditors agree to it and support it in doing so.

sections.label: Expedited procedure for rehabilitation
sections.summary: The new provision aims to minimise expense, formality and delay, letting the company focus resources on rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The aim of this new provision is to minimise the expense, formality and delay in such cases, and the expedited procedure will allow the company to focus its resources on rehabilitation.

sections.label: Judicial manager assigning action proceeds
sections.summary: Clause 99 and the First Schedule give the judicial manager power to assign proceeds of an action to a third party for funding.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 99 and the First Schedule provide for the powers of the judicial manager, including a new power at paragraph (f) of the First Schedule, to assign, in accordance with the prescribed regulations, the proceeds of an action set out in that paragraph.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Currently, a majority of such actions may not be pursued due largely to there being a lack of financial resources.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: These new provisions allow the judicial manager to assign proceeds from such an action to a third party, in exchange for funding of the action.

sections.label: Personal liability not re-enacted
sections.summary: Because personal liability is academic in practice, clause 102 does not re-enact the provision imposing it on judicial managers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: However, the net effect of this practice is that it renders the imposition of personal liability quite academic in the first place.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Therefore, at clause 102 of this Bill, the provision imposing personal liability on judicial managers has not been re-enacted.

sections.label: Restructuring proceedings contract restrictions
sections.summary: Clause 440(1) bars parties from terminating, amending or claiming accelerated payment under agreements solely due to restructuring proceedings or insolvency.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 440(1) provides that no party may by reason only that any restructuring proceedings as defined in clause 440(6) are commenced or that the company is insolvent and thereafter (a) terminate or amend, or claim an accelerated payment or forfeiture of the term under, any agreement with the company; or (b) terminate or modify any right or obligation under any agreement with the company.

sections.label: Judicial management and ipso facto clause
sections.summary: A developer is restricted from relying on the ipso facto clause when the main contractor files for judicial management, but may use it if the contractor also fails construction milestones.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: If the main contractor is in financial distress and files an application to Court to place the company into judicial management, the developer will be restricted by clause 440 from relying on the ipso facto clause, because it is triggered by the filing of the application for a judicial management order, which is one of the specified restructuring proceedings in clause 440(6).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: If, however, in addition to the filing of the restructuring proceedings, the main contractor also fails to meet construction milestones and timelines which are built into the contract, the developer may use the ipso facto clause to terminate the contract or for a variety of other reliefs as specified in the contract.

sections.label: Relief for significant financial hardship
sections.summary: A counterparty may apply to Court for relief on the basis of significant financial hardship.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Second, a counterparty may apply to Court, nonetheless, for relief on the basis of significant financial hardship.

sections.label: Singapore court signs US MOUs
sections.summary: The Supreme Court of Singapore concluded two Memoranda of Understanding with US Bankruptcy Courts for Delaware and the Southern District of New York.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: For example, just last week, the Supreme Court of Singapore concluded two Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) with the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware and the US Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York.

sections.label: New regime for insolvency practitioners
sections.summary: The Bill will introduce a new regulatory regime for insolvency practitioners acting as officeholders in insolvency and restructuring proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In particular, the Bill will introduce a new regulatory regime for insolvency practitioners acting as officeholders in insolvency and restructuring proceedings.

sections.label: Conditions imposed on insolvency practitioners
sections.summary: The question asks what other conditions the Government intends to impose on all insolvency practitioners, besides qualifications and stated conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One, besides having the right qualifications, such as being a solicitor, public or chartered accountant, which are provided in clause 50, and besides the conditions stated in clause 56(b) to (l), what are the other conditions which the Government intends to impose on all insolvency practitioners?

sections.label: Compliance costs under new regime
sections.summary: The question asks the Senior Minister of State about expected compliance costs for practitioners and whether this will increase business costs for companies in insolvency proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Next, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State, with the new regulatory regime, what are the expected costs of compliance by practitioners, and will that lead to increased business costs for companies involved in insolvency proceedings one way or another?

sections.label: Bankruptcy applications after threshold increase
sections.summary: MinLaw data shows bankruptcy applications dipped in the first year after the threshold rose from $10,000 to $15,000, then rose again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to data I have found on the MinLaw website for the number of bankruptcy applications for the past two years after the new bankruptcy threshold was increased from $10,000 to $15,000, the number dipped in the first year and then rose again.

sections.label: Insolvency practitioner licensing regime
sections.summary: The Bill's licensing regime expands the inquiry beyond a fraud or dishonesty conviction to civil judgments and other offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A main feature of this Bill is the licensing regime for insolvency practitioners in Division 3 of Part 3.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Previously, it was a blanket ban against anyone who had "been convicted of an offence involving fraud or dishonesty punishable on conviction by imprisonment for three months or more." The Bill expands the inquiry to having a judgment in civil proceedings involving a finding of fraud, dishonesty or breach of fiduciary duty; or conviction of an offence in Singapore or elsewhere of any offence involving fraud, dishonesty or moral turpitude.

sections.label: Secured creditor interest notification
sections.summary: Clause 327(4)(A) requires a secured creditor to notify an intention to claim interest on the debt after a bankruptcy order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Under clause 327(4)(A), a secured creditor is required to notify an intention to claim interest in respect of his or her debt after a bankruptcy order is made.

sections.label: Restriction of ipso facto clauses
sections.summary: Clause 440 restricts ipso facto clauses in relation to judicial management and schemes of arrangement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The second is clause 440, which restricts ipso facto clauses in relation to judicial management and schemes of arrangement.

sections.label: Commencement of winding up and provable debts
sections.summary: Clause 126(2) defines commencement of winding up as the time of the winding up application, raising questions about the reference point for provable debts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Clause 126(2) defines commencement of winding up as “the time of the making of the application for the winding up.” In contrast, the current section 87(1) of the Bankruptcy Act on which clause 218(1) is based reads “the following are provable in bankruptcy: (a) any debt or liability to which a bankrupt (i) is subject at the date of the bankruptcy order; or (ii) may become subject before the bankrupt’s discharge by reason of any obligation incurred before the date of the bankruptcy order.” Therefore, as seen by the current section 59 of the Bankruptcy Act, the bankruptcy order and bankruptcy application are different.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Whether or not the reference point for provable debts is from a winding up order or from commencement of winding up, that is, the winding up application, has practical implications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Halsbury’s Laws of Singapore point out “if the legal position is such that a person cannot prove for a debt incurred after he has knowledge of a winding up application, a company’s business would effectively be paralysed by the filing of a winding up application… since a prudent businessman is unlikely to deal with a company which is the subject of a winding up application.” As not all applications for winding up end in an order for winding up and since not all judicial management cases will end in winding up, was it intended for the law on provability of debts to change its reference point from the making of the winding up order on the one hand to the making of such applications on the other?

sections.label: Refining debt restructuring processes
sections.summary: The Bill caps amendments positioning Singapore as an international debt restructuring centre, and processes should continue to be refined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Even as this Bill is a capstone to the preceding amendments which strategically positioned Singapore to be an international debt restructuring centre, it is important, just as these amendments have done, to continue to refine the processes for clarity, better calibration and balancing of interests.

sections.label: MinLaw consultation on insolvency amendments
sections.summary: The speaker applauds MinLaw's long consultative process, noting 70 amendments and about 150 recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I applaud MinLaw for leading the consultative process over such a long period of time, getting feedback from the players in this industry and implementing the recommendations that have been made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But it is worth the wait because we can see the complexities involved: 70 amendments through various statutes, about 150 recommendations have been provided to the Ministries for consideration.

sections.label: Judicial management and secured creditors
sections.summary: The speaker asks how to balance financial centre reputation with debt restructuring aims given weakened secured creditor rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Also, in relation to judicial management, it is now easier to get judicial management orders and the rights of the secured creditors have been watered down consequently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is in this context that I wish to seek an explanation from the learned Senior Minister of State: how do we strike a balance between the need to maintain our reputation as a financial centre and our intent to build Singapore as an international centre for debt restructuring?

sections.label: Carve-outs for eligible financial contracts
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarification on section 440 exceptions and asks whether the industry was consulted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The hon Senior Minister of State mentioned that there could be carve-outs in relation to eligible financial contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I seek clarification as to what are the exceptions that may apply in relation to section 440 and, in that regard, I note section 440(5) contemplates a carve-out for eligible financial contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask whether the industry has been consulted on this provision and, in particular, because both in the 2013 and 2016 reports referred to earlier, this provision was not specifically recommended.

sections.label: Single legislation brings clarity
sections.summary: A single piece of legislation brings clarity, access, expediency, cost-effectiveness and certainty by reducing cross-referencing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Indeed, having them in a single piece of legislation will bring greater clarity and access, as well as expediency, cost-effectiveness and certainty through the reduction of numerous cross-referencing that we now see between the Companies Act and the Bankruptcy Act.

sections.label: Licensing regime for insolvency practitioners
sections.summary: A robust licensing and regulatory regime is necessary to maintain professional standards among insolvency practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To develop and strengthen Singapore as a restructuring forum of choice, a robust licensing and regulatory regime forms an integral and necessary part of the ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is necessary to ensure that professional standards are maintained and upheld by all insolvency practitioners.

sections.label: Clause 58(3) criminal offence
sections.summary: Clause 58(3) makes failure to comply with a written direction the offence, not breach of licence conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Clause 58(3) provides that it is the failure to comply with the requirement specified in the written direction issued under clause 58(1) that constitutes the criminal offence, and not the failure to comply with the condition of the licence per se.

sections.label: Offence for breaching written direction
sections.summary: The offence is failing to comply with a written direction, not the initial failure to comply with a licence condition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, if there is contravention or if there is a non-compliance, the direction would specify that such compliance has to be provided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And it is a subsequent failure to comply with that written direction that constitutes the offence, and not the initial failure to comply with the condition of the licence.

sections.label: Court orders before third-party funding
sections.summary: Clause 204(2) lets the Court make orders before a creditor provides funding or indemnity, increasing third-party funding availability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To address this, the new provision in clause 204(2) allows the Court to make such orders prior to the creditor providing the funding or indemnity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In summary, these two options will increase the availability of third-party funding to facilitate the judicial manager or liquidator pursuing claims against parties on behalf of the company.

sections.label: Debt restructuring and financial centre
sections.summary: Being an international centre for debt restructuring augments Singapore's attractiveness as a global financial centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Being an international centre for debt restructuring, in fact, augments our attractiveness as a global financial centre.

sections.label: Clause 440 restricts contract termination rights
sections.summary: Clause 440 prevents a contract party from unilaterally terminating or modifying a contract solely because restructuring proceedings commenced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That is why it did not make it into the 2017 amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But the restriction that we have in mind in clause 440 supports a company's restructuring efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It prevents the other party to the contract from unilaterally exercising his or her rights against a company to terminate or modify the contract solely because of the commencement of restructuring proceedings.

sections.label: Restriction is suspensory in nature
sections.summary: The restriction lasts only while the company is in restructuring proceedings, from commencement until it exits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: First, the restriction is suspensory in nature, meaning it is only for the duration of the period when the company has embarked on and continues the restructuring proceedings, so from the time it commences until the time it gets out of the restructuring proceedings, either successfully or unsuccessfully.

sections.label: When contractual rights are restricted
sections.summary: Contractual rights are restricted only if restructuring proceedings are commenced or the company is insolvent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The exercise of contractual rights is only restricted if restructuring proceedings are commenced, or the company is insolvent.

sections.label: Eligible financial contracts definition
sections.summary: The definition of eligible financial contracts likely includes repurchase agreements, swap agreements and forward contracts, similar to the US position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: At this juncture, I can say that it is likely that the definition of "eligible financial contracts" that will be exempted would include repurchase agreements, swap agreements and forward contracts, which is similar to the position in the US.

sections.label: Creditor safeguard for financial hardship
sections.summary: Clause 440(4) allows any affected creditor to apply to Court on the basis of significant financial hardship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Next, clause 440(4) contains a further safeguard for creditors by allowing any affected creditor to apply to Court on the basis of significant financial hardship.

sections.label: Secured creditor interest notification
sections.summary: Clause 327(4) requires a secured creditor to notify the Official Assignee within 30 days of the bankruptcy order of intent to claim interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Next, I turn to the point Mr Christopher de Souza raised about clause 327(4), which requires a secured creditor to notify the Official Assignee within 30 days after the date of the bankruptcy order of the intention to claim interest on the secured creditor’s debt.

sections.label: Judicial management debt priority
sections.summary: Clause 114 gives priority to debts incurred by the judicial manager, including employees' wages, ahead of other expenses and the judicial manager's remuneration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Given that there are various types of debts incurred during the course of judicial management, including employees' wages, clause 114 contains new provisions that clearly provide for the priority of such a debt incurred by the judicial manager on behalf of the company ahead of other expenses incurred or the remuneration of the judicial manager.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Under this new provision, employees' wages that are incurred in the course of judicial management would fall under clause 114(1)(b) as, and I quote, "any sums payable in respect of any debts or liabilities of the company incurred during judicial management".

sections.label: Employees' claims priority in liquidation
sections.summary: Clause 203(1)(d) and (e) gives employees' claims the next highest priority among all preferential debts of a company in liquidation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Immediately after the preferential debts mentioned in clause 203(1)(a) to (c), clause 203(1)(d) and (e) provides that employees’ claims enjoy the next highest priority as among all the preferential debts of the company in liquidation.

sections.label: Clause 203 preferential claims split
sections.summary: Clause 203 splits former priority claims into three portions, with no change to the relative position of employees' claims under section 328(1).

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, what clause 203 has sought to do is to break up what otherwise used to be a group of priority or preferential claims, all of which already ranked ahead of employees' wages, and parcel that out into three separate portions to deal with it in (a), (b) and (c) of clause 203(1).

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Those debts that were previously under section 328(1)(a) have been set out in those three provisions which I have mentioned and there is, therefore, no change from the existing position under section 328(1), in relation to the relative position of the employees’ claims.

sections.label: Liquidator Ewe Pang Kooi trial
sections.summary: Mr Ewe Pang Kooi acted as liquidator for 21 companies and was on trial for allegedly pocketing over $40 million from them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: One example will be Mr Ewe Pang Kooi.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: He acted as a liquidator for 21 companies and he was on trial earlier this year for allegedly pocketing more than $40 million from those companies.

sections.label: Cross-border insolvency mechanisms used
sections.summary: About 100 applications followed the 2017 amendments, using the UNCITRAL Model Law and the Judiciary Insolvency Network with the US, Korea and Australia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As I mentioned at my opening speech, we had about 100 applications made following the amendments in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, we have used UNCITRAL Model Law on Cross-Border Insolvency, which is a cross-border mechanism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We have the Judiciary Insolvency Network (JIN), where Courts in Singapore can now, in real-time, link up with and also speak with courts of other jurisdictions and, so far, the US, Korea and Australia are jurisdictions that have signed up for the scheme and that allows our Courts here to be very global and very cross-border in the kind of work and the kind of cases that they see.

sections.label: Restructuring ecosystem and ipso facto feedback
sections.summary: Singapore will continue developing its restructuring and insolvency ecosystem, and stakeholder engagement on ipso facto clauses continued after the report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Beyond the legal regime, we will continue to develop and enhance Singapore’s ecosystem for restructuring and insolvency so that Singapore remains efficient, effective and consistent in achieving outcomes that are in the interests of all stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Murali Pillai asked if we had received feedback on ipso facto clauses, in particular, that, as you know, was not in the report but subsequently we continued with the engagement of stakeholders.

sections.label: Monitoring issues not yet dealt with
sections.summary: Matters already addressed were addressed today, while those not yet dealt with are taken onboard and will continue to be monitored.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Those that I have addressed, I have addressed today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Those that we have not yet been in a position to deal with, I have taken onboard and we will continue to monitor them as we look at refining these in the near future.
